items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: I think Benny Goodman was the first one to present them to the public when he had Teddy and Hamp-- Lionel, in his quartet, Gene.

ctx.x: I never took it, never concentrate on it that serious, because I never come in contact with it that much, as far as playing was concerned. I knew that the colored musicians, we had just millions of them, fabulous, could play in Harlem. You could go right next door and hear the damndest horn blowing things you ever heard in your life, drummers, Big Sid Catlett, all them guys, Jabbo on trumpet, sure, Sidney DeParis and all them guys, sharks, because they had to be because it was a jungle. Everybody waiting for you…
I think Benny Goodman was the first one to present them to the public when he had Teddy and Hamp-- Lionel, in his quartet, Gene.

When you were coming up, like you were living in Washington, how did the Negro musicians look at -- how did they see the music scene. I mean, did they feel like they were getting the proper breaks, or did they feel --
